rubrics.date: Missale Romanum 1962, Proper of Saints, 30 April: S. Catharinae Senensis Virginis. These three orations belong to this observance when it is commemorated in the Mass of the Vigil of the Ascension; this record does not select the saint's own Mass. The observance is not transferred (Rubricae generales 31, 94–95).
rubrics.scope: Mass only: the Collect, Secret and Postcommunion follow the corresponding orations of the Vigil of the Ascension. This relation does not infer an Office, a local calendar, a procession or any other preliminary ceremony.
rubrics.rank: An ordinary commemoration (Rubricae generales 107–109), made in low Mass and conventual Mass, but not in a sung Mass that is not conventual (108, 111 a).
rubrics.admission: The second-class Vigil takes precedence over third- and fourth-class observances (Rubricae generales 31; the table at 91, place 21). It admits one commemoration (111 c, 434); the ordinary commemoration is omitted in a non-conventual sung Mass (111 a). This record is limited to its named date beneath that Vigil, not a general fixed-date saint calendar.
rubrics.conclusion: For the Mass oration followed by this single commemoration, each has its own conclusion (Rubricae generales 436–437). At the Secret, the Mass oration and its conclusion are said quietly; only the final Secret's concluding Per omnia saecula saeculorum and the response Amen are audible (480–481). This does not prescribe a separate conclusion for every intermediate oration when more prayers are present.
